finding: THE ACTIONABLE PART DID NOT SURVIVE, AND I HAD BEEN LOOKING IN THE WRONG PLACE
verify_quoted: for each such tool, a test that truncates its output to a small budget and asserts the actionable part SURVIVES.
my_earlier_answer_was_wrong: the first sweep tested DISCLOSURE and reported that most tools 'cannot be budget-squeezed through their own interface' because only 2 of 27 accept a `limit` argument. The squeeze is not an argument. It is Engine._compact_closed_observations, which cuts EVERY observation to CLOSED_OBSERVATION_CHARS = 500 as HEAD 250 + marker + TAIL ~208, eliding the middle -- and it applies to every tool whether or not it takes a limit. The budget was always reachable; I was testing the wrong layer.
who_was_losing_its_own_scope: odyssey.selection_brief -- 14,614 chars, and I had shipped it ONE HOUR EARLIER
what_that_costs_a_round: the round receives rows and cannot tell how many exist or whether it has them all. That is exactly how round 20 read a partial census as complete and called an already-MEASURED axis 'worst owed'. The affordance defect I fixed in the census was one instance of a class.

the_fix.rule: lead with the keys that say HOW MUCH -- n, total, count, shown, truncated, n_owed, n_ranked, n_specimens, specimen_count -- before the rows that say WHAT, so the head 250 chars carry the scope.
applied_at: the two shared odyssey read factories (_odyssey_read and _odyssey_read_verb), which covers ingest, status, queue, value, economics and the read-only verbs in one change
the_fix.note: _lead_with already existed for exactly this and had 7 call sites. This is the same move applied BY RULE instead of by remembering, which is the difference between a habit and a control.

verification.mutation: _scope_first reduced to dict(payload) -> 3 tools go SCOPE_LOST again and OK falls 12 -> 9. Restored; markers grep 0.
verification.regression: the disclosure sweep still passes; hcli/test_engine_tool_loop.py 20 passed
verification.why_only_3_of_5_return_under_mutation: two of the five now route through the shared odyssey factories, whose ordering the mutation does not reach in the same way -- the fix there is structural rather than per-call.

the_15_with_no_scope_field: NOT counted as defects. They return no row list, so there is no 'how many' to lose. The earlier sweep established that separately.
scar: THE BUDGET WAS NOT AN ARGUMENT, IT WAS A LAYER. When a test says a thing cannot be squeezed, check what actually squeezes it in production.

coverage_was_widened.why: the verify says 'for EACH such tool'. The first sweep covered 28 zero-argument tools of 72 and excluded every read-only tool that takes an argument -- which is not the same as covering them.
coverage_was_widened.how: real, harmless arguments: a file that exists, a pattern that matches, a catalog focus. Not synthetic fixtures -- the point is what the tool actually returns.
coverage_was_widened.finding: the argumented tools ALREADY lead with their scope -- _truncation_fields was applied there long ago. Widening found no new defect, which is itself worth recording: the file-reading path had this right and the collection-returning path did not.

what_remains_uncovered: mutating, costly and networked tools are not exercised by an automated sweep, and tools whose required arguments cannot be synthesized safely (shell.readonly, vmcp.query, odyssey.patient, the anatomy tools which need a real snapshot directory) are excluded by name rather than silently. 34 of 72 registered tools are covered.
